_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401884736.overall: Bayern are top with 21 points from nine games and host 15th-placed Cologne, who have not won in four league games and scored only two goals in that run. Vincent Kompany returns to the touchline for the first time since collapsing on 23 October; at Thursday's press conference he said Musiala is available and will probably be involved, while Luis Díaz is not ready yet (he hopes within seven days) and Davies, Neuer, Gnabry and Saibari stay out, all already counted by the numbers. Cologne's René Wagner is without Dallinga, Hübers, Skhiri, van den Berg and Rondic (all counted) and is expected to set up with a back five, with Ache fit but likely on the bench. Robin Braun referees, and his above-average card record is already in the numbers. Match-day check: no new injuries or surprises, so the view is unchanged.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and already take about 12% off Bayern's attack for Díaz and Musiala as if both are fully out. Kompany confirmed on Thursday that Díaz is still a week away but Musiala is available and will probably play some part, which the numbers don't see, so I nudge up just 1%, to about 3.74. Cologne without Dallinga and Skhiri is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, with Bayern's recent run of corners (37 in six) already added. Cologne are expected to line up with a back five and defend deep, then break quickly, which is the one-sided pattern the numbers already expect, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add about 9% for referee Robin Braun (4.4 cards a game against a 3.9 average) plus Cologne's high recent card count (17 in six). Wagner wants his players to 'go where it hurts', but that fits the same pattern the numbers count, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots and already add 7.5% for Bayern's hot shooting run (127 shots in six). Bayern's attack around Kane, Olise, Karl and Brown is near full strength apart from Díaz, who is counted, so I stay at 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.4 shots on target, already lifted 11% for Bayern's recent accuracy. Musiala off the bench adds a little, but that is in the small goals nudge, and Cologne's weak attack without Dallinga is counted, so I stay at 12.4.

401884732.overall: Union are 16th with 7 points and only 48 shots in their last six, and Mauro Lustrinelli's side host Leipzig, 4th with four wins in five after a 5-2 win over Augsburg. Union's injury news got worse overnight: the Berliner Zeitung (19 Nov) reports Juranovic ill, so the numbers are right to count him out (about -8% on Union's goals), while Ligainsider reports Janik Haberer, Union's top scorer this season per Sports Mole, out with an illness and Burcu missing training; Uduokhai, Nsoki and Skov are out, and captain Trimmel is back. The numbers count Juranovic, Skov and Nsoki but not Haberer or Uduokhai. Leipzig miss Guiu and Ouedraogo (counted), with the Bundesliga's predicted XI built around Nusa, Nkunku, Gruda and Romulo. Christian Dingert referees; his near-average record (3.8 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take about 8% off Union for Juranovic, who the Berliner Zeitung now reports ill, so that cut holds. What they don't see is Haberer, Union's top scorer, out ill and Burcu doubtful, for a side that has scored little lately, so I go 5% lower, to about 2.8 (was -3, when Juranovic looked set to return).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already cut for both sides' low recent corner counts (Union 18, Leipzig 22 in six). Leipzig win their corners down the flanks through Nusa and Raum and Union rely on long balls and set pieces whoever plays, which the numbers already see, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards and already add Union's rough recent run (18 cards in six) while trimming a little for referee Dingert, who shows about 3.8 a game. Lustrinelli wants an intense, brave Union, and Trimmel's return adds an experienced defender, but that is the same pattern the numbers already add for, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots and already cut Union's shots 13% for their recent drought. Haberer, their top scorer, is out ill and Burcu is doubtful, and Juranovic's crosses from the left are also missing, so Union's attack is thinner than the numbers assume; I go 4% lower, to about 24.1 (was -3).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, with Leipzig's recent accuracy (+8%) and Union's poor one (11 on target in six) already counted. Losing Haberer, Union's most reliable finisher, takes away some of their few good chances, so I go 4% lower, to about 8.9 (was -3).

401884735.overall: Leverkusen are 5th with 16 points and host Paderborn, 13th but unbeaten in four with the league's best defensive start in their history (11 conceded). Carles Martinez has most of his attack back: Sports Mole's preview and the Bundesliga's predicted XI both have Diaby and Maza starting behind Schick (eight goals), while Bulinews expects Kofane and Tella back too and Sports Mole still lists Tella, Terrier and Kofane out. The numbers count Diaby, Tella, Doue, Terrier and Eichhorn as missing, so Diaby's return is the clear thing they miss. Paderborn's coach Ralf Kettemann expects a game 'focused on defending our own goal'; they miss Gayret, with Hoffmeier, Klaas and others counted. Tobias Reichel referees and his near-average record (4.0 a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and take about 3% off Leverkusen for Diaby, who two predicted lineups now have starting, with Maza cleared after his Algeria knock. Paderborn plan to defend deep and have conceded only 11 in nine, and reports differ on Kofane and Tella, so I go only 3% higher, to about 2.7 (was +4).

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with Leverkusen expected to win about 8 against a Paderborn back three that will sit deep. Diaby and Maza returning changes who finishes moves more than how often Leverkusen reach the byline, so I stay at 11.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, with referee Reichel (4.0 a game) adding about 3%. Paderborn's low recent card count is already in the numbers, and a deep block facing lots of possession usually means fouls when chasing, which their record also shows, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already lifted slightly for both sides' recent volume. Leverkusen kept shooting a lot (102 in six) even with forwards missing, so Diaby's and Maza's returns mostly help quality, not volume, and I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. With Diaby back on the right and Maza at number 10 behind Schick, Leverkusen's finishing options are better than the numbers assume, though Paderborn's tight defence limits clear looks, so I go 2% higher, to about 10.5 (was +3).

401884731.overall: Bottom side Gladbach (4 points, the league's worst defence with 25 conceded) host Dortmund, 2nd, unbeaten, level with Bayern and with the league's best defence (7 conceded). Gladbach are without the banned Itakura and the injured Kleindienst, Leopold, Leszczynski and Ullrich; the numbers count Bolin and Ullrich for goals, though Sports Mole's predicted XI has Bolin starting while the Bundesliga's does not. For Dortmund, Can, Konstantelias and Lerma are out, and Guirassy, Anton and Chukwuemeka were late fitness calls (BVB site, Bulinews); Sports Mole now expects Guirassy on the bench with Fabio Silva leading the line, while Anton is in both predicted XIs. Alexander Blessin expects a fight and Niko Kovac warned against underestimating Gladbach. Robert Hartmann referees and his record (4.0 a game) is close to average.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already taking Bolin and Ullrich off Gladbach. What they can't see is Guirassy, Dortmund's main striker, likely starting on the bench after his muscle problem, with Fabio Silva expected to lead the line, and Gladbach still without captain Kleindienst; I go 3% lower, to about 2.7 (was -2).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already nudged up for Dortmund's recent count (37 in six). Gladbach play a back three and look to break, and Dortmund build through their wing-backs, both of which the numbers already expect, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards and already add a big 22% for Gladbach's recent card spike (21 in six), including Itakura's sending-off that bans him here. Blessin wants a fight in a full stadium, but that is the same pattern the numbers already add for, and referee Hartmann is close to average, so I stay at 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting (Gladbach 93, Dortmund 96 in six). Kovac plans to play his fit first-choice players, so a Guirassy-less attack changes who shoots more than how often, and I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. Guirassy, Dortmund's most accurate finisher, is likely only a bench option and Gladbach miss Kleindienst, so both sides' best shooters are short of a start, and I go 3% lower, to about 9.4 (was -2).

401884734.overall: Frankfurt (10th) and Hoffenheim (9th) are level on 12 points in a mid-table game with little extra at stake; the last 11 meetings all had at least four goals and both teams scored in the last 13 (Bundesliga.com). Adi Huetter is without the banned Elias Baum (counted), Koch is fit again, but Can Uzun came back from international duty with a cold and hessenschau (19 Nov) expects him to miss out, which the numbers don't know. Hoffenheim's defence is thin, with Hajdari, Hranac, Gendrey and De Cat out, and the numbers only count these for Frankfurt's goals through Conte's line, not the defenders; one hessenschau headline (20 Nov) says Hoffenheim have Bambase Conte back, though the numbers take about 11% off their goals for him. Max Burda referees; his short record is just below average and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals and take about 11% off Hoffenheim for Conte, whom one hessenschau report says is back, while they give Frankfurt nothing for Hoffenheim's four missing defenders. Uzun's likely absence costs Frankfurt some creativity, and Conte's return rests on one source, so I go 4% higher, to about 3.7 (was +2).

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, already nudged up for Hoffenheim's recent count (37 in six). A reshuffled Hoffenheim back line may concede more chances but not clearly more corners, and both sides press high rather than camp on the flanks, so I stay at 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards, with recent counts, head-to-head and referee Burda's slightly low record already in them. Huetter and Ilzer both expect a high-intensity, aggressive game (Koch calls intensity the key factor), but both teams always play that way and it is in their records, so I stay at 3.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots and already add Hoffenheim's recent volume (101 in six, +12%). Their gaps at the back affect chance quality more than the total, and Uzun's absence trims Frankfurt's long-range shooting, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. Hoffenheim's makeshift defence should give Frankfurt's strikers Ebnoutalib and Burkardt cleaner looks, and Conte may be back up front, partly offset by losing Uzun, so I go 2% higher, to about 10.3 (was 0).

401884728.overall: Promoted Elversberg (7th, 13 points, unbeaten at home except against Bayern per Julian Schuster) host Freiburg (3rd, 19 points, three wins in their last four including 2-0 over Union) in the clubs' first league meeting. Elversberg have conceded 18 goals in nine and their first-choice centre-backs are in doubt: the Bundesliga's predicted XI pairs Rohr and Le Joncour, without Seifert and captain Pinckert. Right-back Gyamerah, whom the numbers count as out (adding about 6% to Freiburg's goals), is in that predicted XI. Freiburg miss Muslija (counted) and the banned Berkay Yilmaz, not a regular, and are expected with Beste, Suzuki and Matanovic. Richard Hempel referees with only two games on record, which the numbers blend towards the average.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals and add about 6% to Freiburg's goals for Gyamerah being out, but he is in the predicted XI, so that boost is too big. Elversberg are also likely without both first-choice centre-backs, Seifert and Pinckert, which the numbers don't see, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, with Freiburg's recent run of corners (30 in six) already added. Freiburg's wide play through Beste and Treu wins most of their corners and Elversberg concede plenty (44 in six), both in the numbers, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. Referee Hempel has only two games on record, which the numbers already blend towards the average, and neither side's recent card counts stand out; a stand-in centre-back pairing for Elversberg is only a small hunch for more fouls, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with Freiburg expected to shoot more. Elversberg have allowed 103 shots in their last six and Freiburg have been shooting above their usual level; both are already counted, so I keep 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Freiburg's accuracy has dipped lately (already counted), and the centre-back doubts at Elversberg and Gyamerah's return pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 8.4.

401884729.overall: Schalke (17th, 6 points, seven games without a win in all competitions) host Stuttgart (8th, 12 points, two league wins in a row) at 18:30 in front of about 60,000; Schalke have still not scored a home goal this season, though they have conceded just 11. Moussa Sylla is back in the squad for the first time since matchday 5 and may start, with Gantenbein and Bachmann also available (90min, Sky, Flashscore), while top scorer Robin Gosens, back in partial training after his knee knock, is at best a bench option; Becker and Woeber are out and already counted. Stuttgart are still without Angelo Stiller (adductor) and Luca Jaquez (rib), both on the numbers' list, while Josha Vagnoman is back in team training and Leo Sauer trained fully on Thursday; Stuttgart play at Inter in the Champions League on Wednesday. Sebastian Hoeness expects a passionate Schalke and wants high intensity and runs in behind; Daniel Siebert referees, and his slightly higher card record is already added.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off for Woeber at Schalke and for Stiller and Vagnoman at Stuttgart. Gosens, Schalke's top scorer, is not expected to start, which the numbers can't see, but Sylla's return up front and Vagnoman being back in training soften that, so I trim only 2%, to about 2.06.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Stuttgart expected to win about 6 of them. Schalke defend deep and look to counter, which hands visitors corners, and Hoeness wants his side to run in behind and down the wings, but both habits are already in the teams' records, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards and already add about 8% for referee Daniel Siebert (4.1 a game) plus a little for Schalke's recent games. Hoeness expects a physical, passionate home side in front of 60,000, but that is how Schalke play every home game and it is in their record, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. Schalke's attack produces few shots and will likely start without Gosens, and Stuttgart still miss their main midfield passer Stiller, whom the numbers count only for goals, not shot volume; Sylla's return gives Schalke a target up front, so the trim stays small, 2%, to about 27.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already cut Schalke's for their poor recent accuracy (13 on target in six). Gosens unlikely to start and Stiller out make both build-ups a bit poorer, while Sylla's comeback gives Schalke a finisher back, so I trim 2%, to about 9.4.

401884733.overall: Two struggling sides meet at the WWK Arena: Augsburg (14th, 9 points) are seven games without a win under Manuel Baum after a 5-2 loss at Leipzig, and Mainz (12th, 10 points) have lost four competitive games in a row, including a cup exit at Bochum. The Bundesliga's preview lists Augsburg without Banks, Brackelmann (ill), Massengo, Matsima and Mounie, and Mainz without Kohr and Silas; the numbers now count all of these for goals, including about +6% on Mainz's goals for each missing Augsburg defender. Urs Fischer calls Augsburg compact, quick on the break and dangerous at set pieces, while Mainz's Tietz leads the attack. Martin Petersen referees; his high card record (4.5 a game, +14%) is already in the numbers, as is both sides' leaky recent form.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already lifted by both leaky defences' recent form and now counting Brackelmann, Massengo and Matsima out (Augsburg lose some goals, Mainz gain about 6% per missing defender). Last night's lean up was for exactly those absences, which the numbers now carry, so I drop it and stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Augsburg winning slightly more at home and Mainz's wing-backs Caci and Mwene back to push wide. Both teams are predicted in a back three with wing-backs, which matches their records, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, already including about 14% for referee Petersen and Mainz's high recent count. Mainz's combative holding midfielder Kohr is out until the new year and Augsburg's Massengo also misses out; the numbers count both only for goals, not their bookings, so I trim 3%, to about 5.0, kept small because Baum expects a duel-heavy game.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already lifted by Augsburg's big recent volume (+19%) and Mainz's (+7%). Fischer expects a compact Augsburg playing on the break, which fits their record, so I stay at 31.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with momentum adding for both (+13% Augsburg, +6% Mainz). The reshuffled Augsburg back line that made me lean higher last night is now in the numbers through the missing defenders, so I drop the +3 and stay at 10.8.

401884730.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 points, unbeaten at home) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 points); Werder have won eight of the last nine top-flight meetings at the Weserstadion, and Fuellkrug leads the league with nine goals, six from set pieces. Werder's creator Marco Gruell (calf; two goals and eight assists) is the big doubt: he went off at Stuttgart with a long-standing calf problem (90min, 8 Nov), last night's report had Thioune saying he had not trained, though the Bundesliga's predicted XI still lists him; Weiser (thigh) is out and counted. Hamburg are without Remberg, Nadir, Torunarigha, Sambi Lokonga and captain Poulsen (the numbers count Poulsen and Sambi Lokonga for goals), with Daka and Muheim, who has three long-range goals, in the predicted XI. Florian Badstuebner referees: his low card record (-23%) and the derby boost (+39%) are both in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already taking about 12% off Hamburg for Poulsen and 3% for Sambi Lokonga, and 4% off Werder for Weiser. They do not count Gruell, Werder's main creator, who is a real doubt with his calf; sources disagree on whether he starts, so I go 4% lower, to about 2.6 (was -6), with Fuellkrug's set pieces still a threat.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Werder expected to win most of them at home against Hamburg's back three with wing-backs. With or without Gruell, Werder's wide play and Fuellkrug's set-piece threat drive their corners, which the numbers see, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards: they add 39% for the derby but take 23% off for referee Badstuebner, who shows only 3.1 cards a game, and both sides have been booked less than usual lately (counted). Thioune and Polzin are old colleagues and nothing in the news points to extra needle beyond the derby itself, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20%), much of it built through Gruell. With him doubtful and Weiser out on the right, Werder may lose two of their main suppliers, so I take 2% off, to about 30.6 (was -3, now that his absence is less certain).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six games already added (+15%). If Gruell, who has set up eight goals, misses out, Werder's chances should be fewer and less clean; as he is only doubtful, I take 3% off, to about 10.5 (was -4).

401883112.overall: A relegation fight in Encamp on Friday night: FC Andorra are 21st with 11 points and no win in four, Leganés 16th with 15 after beating Burgos 3-1, Luis Carrión's first league win in charge. Andorra are without goalkeeper Jesús Owono (12-match ban) and centre-back Diego Alende (red card), both already in the numbers, plus midfielder Théo Le Normand; reports differ on Gael Alonso (back per Thursday's previews, still a doubt per El Gol Digital). Leganés get Javi Montero back from a ban and Gharbi is an option to start, while one report says Rubén Peña and Pulido have knocks and Carrión called a few players 'a bit iffy'. Carrión wants a high press and useful possession, which could cut into the long spells of Andorra pressure the numbers expect. José Luis Guzmán Mansilla referees, and his low card record is already in the numbers; match-day news changed nothing in the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already add about 6% to Leganés' goals for Alende's ban. Andorra have conceded 24 in 13 and keep giving away early goals, while Leganés have Millán in form and Montero back; but with Gael Alonso back and Bomba expected to start, Andorra's back line is not as patched-up as feared, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 5.8 of them Andorra's, as a home side that usually has the ball and pushes up. Carrión wants Leganés to keep the ball and press high, which could trim Andorra's share a little, but Leganés' recent habit of conceding corners is already in momentum (+3.9%), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards: both sides have been booked a lot lately (+11% and +6.6% momentum) and the referee, José Luis Guzmán Mansilla, averages 4.7 cards a game, which already takes about 13% off. It is a tense game between two bottom-five sides, but the previews point to no extra needle beyond that, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, about 18 of them Andorra's, which assumes Leganés sit deep. Carrión said on Thursday he wants a high press and more action in the opponent's half, and Manso also noted Leganés now keep more of the ball, so Andorra may get fewer long spells of pressure; I trim a little, to about 26.4. Leganés' high shots conceded lately are already in momentum (+7%).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Andorra's recent accuracy already in momentum (+7.4%). With Bomba and Gael Alonso available, Andorra's defence should be close to its usual shape apart from Alende, who is already counted, and the small trim to shots is too little to move this, so I stay at 9.6.

401882299.overall: Sabadell (14th, five league games without a win, only 12 goals in 14 games) host Granada (3rd, six straight league wins, one goal conceded in their last five). Sabadell are unbeaten at home (three wins, three draws), but Ferran Costa has about a third of the squad out: besides Gioacchini (out for the season) and the suspended Català, which the numbers count, Urri, Quadri Liameed, Eneko Aguilar, Codina, Pipa, Xavi Moreno and Nuamah are unavailable, and Costa said the team could barely train this week. Granada have almost everyone: only Casadesús is injured and Owen Emeka is with Spain at the Under-17 World Cup, while Diallo and Arnaiz are back on the bench; Pacheta is expected to repeat the XI that beat Las Palmas and has talked about using three strikers. Referee Rafael Sánchez López shows fewer cards than average and the numbers already take that off.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals and already take off Gioacchini, Sabadell's top scorer with 3 goals, plus their poor recent scoring. I lean slightly lower to about 1.8: Sabadell are also without Urri, Liameed and several other squad players the numbers don't see and barely trained this week, while Granada's back line (Juanjo Flores, Lama, Alberto Flores in goal) has conceded once in five games.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, and they already count both sides' slightly low corner counts lately. Sabadell are direct and strong at set pieces and Granada may push more men forward if Pacheta goes with three strikers, but neither clearly changes the corner count, so I stay at 8.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards: they add a little for Sabadell's high card count (41 yellows and 2 reds this season, Català banned after a red) and take a lot off for referee Rafael Sánchez López, who averages 4.5 cards a game against a league 5.3. Granada are a clean side (25 yellows, no reds); Pacheta calls Sabadell the team that runs the most, which can mean fouls, but nothing here is new to the numbers, so I stay at 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots, with 17.1 for Sabadell after a boost for recent form against Granada. I lean lower to about 25.7: Sabadell's attack is thin with Gioacchini, Urri, Liameed and others out and a disrupted week of training, and Granada have been very hard to create against lately.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. Sabadell have put only 17 on target in their last six and now lose more attacking players the numbers don't know about, while Granada have conceded once in five games, so I trim it to about 7.5.

401883108.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Real Sociedad II (18th, 13 points, three unbeaten after six straight defeats) host Cádiz (20th, 11 points), who have not won away in 12 league games. Jon Ansotegi's side lists Ander Barrenetxea as injured and Mamadou Sarr, Beitia, Marchal and Dani Díaz as doubts; the numbers count only Jon Balda's ban (one preview still names Balda in the XI, so treat that as unclear). Cádiz lose Sergio Arribas to a fifth yellow card, reported by two outlets and not in the numbers, but get Jandro Orellana, Bojan Kovacevic and Álvaro García Pascual back; Borja Jiménez says his side lacks accuracy in transitions. Referee Saúl Ais Reig is close to the league average on cards and the numbers add a little for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already adjusting for Balda's ban on both sides and two past meetings. I lean slightly lower to about 2.6: Cádiz have scored little away and now lose Sergio Arribas to suspension, Real Sociedad II have several attackers doubtful, and a relegation clash between two nervous sides tends to be tight; Orellana's return to Cádiz's midfield partly offsets it.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners and already add for Real Sociedad II's high corner count in their last six (38). I found nothing that changes how either side wins corners, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards and already add a bit for referee Saúl Ais Reig (5.5 a game) and recent form. I lean slightly higher to about 5.6 because this is a bottom-of-the-table six-pointer the numbers carry no stakes adjustment for, and Cádiz have players near bans (Borja Vázquez is one yellow from a suspension).

shots.text: The numbers say 27.3 shots, already boosting Real Sociedad II strongly for 98 shots in their last six and trimming Cádiz for their weak attacking form. Arribas's absence and the young hosts' doubts point slightly down but the momentum figures already reflect much of this, so I stay at 27.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, with Cádiz trimmed for 19 on target in their last six. Without Arribas Cádiz lose some creativity, but García Pascual is back up front, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 8.3.

401882301.overall: Castellón (2nd, 30 points, unbeaten at home, only 5 goals conceded in 13 games) can go top with a win over Eldense (16th), who ended a three-game losing run by beating Sabadell. Castellón's top scorer Israel Suero (6 of their 24 goals) is out with a physical problem, confirmed by Pablo Hernández on Friday and not counted by the numbers; Fran Castillo and Rodrigo Rêgo are also out besides Brignani, and today's Castellón Plaza preview says a virus has hit several players, with the coach deciding on them at the last minute, while Matías Orozco is back from Colombia duty. Eldense lose captain Jesús Clemente (dislocated shoulder) and Fidel Chaves (muscle problem), neither counted by the numbers, while Guirao is fit again; Javi Calleja plans to press man-to-man, contest possession and take risks. It is a regional match with a tribute to Jesús de Miguel, and referee Pablo Morales Moreno is slightly below average on cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, 2.0 of them for Castellón. I lean lower because Israel Suero, scorer of a quarter of Castellón's league goals, is out and the numbers don't know it, and today's preview adds a virus in the Castellón squad; Eldense are also without Fidel Chaves and Castellón's defence has conceded only 5 in 13, so I go 8% lower, to about 2.6 (a point more than before because of the virus).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners and already trim Eldense for 19 corners in their last six. Castellón are one of the sides that keep the ball most and should still pin Eldense back even without Suero, while Eldense's plan to contest possession cuts the other way, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards: they add a lot for Eldense's recent cards (20 in six) and take a little off for referee Pablo Morales Moreno (4.6 a game in 7 games). I lean slightly higher to about 5.5 because it is a regional match the numbers do not flag as a derby and Calleja wants aggressive man-to-man pressing all over the pitch, which tends to bring fouls.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots and already trim Castellón for a quieter recent spell. Without Suero, and with a virus going through the squad, Castellón lose some of their attacking edge, and Eldense will try to slow the game by contesting the ball, so I trim 4%, to about 23.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Suero's absence matters most here, since he is the player who turns Castellón's possession into efforts on goal, and the reported virus may weaken their attack further, so I lower it 6%, to about 8.2.

401883107.overall: Tenerife (13th, 18 points, a game in hand) host Mallorca (7th, one point off the play-offs) in the second home game since the death of former player Jesús de Miguel, whom Mallorca honoured at the stadium on Friday. Both sides are tired: Tenerife play their third game in six days after beating Ceuta and winning 2-5 at Badajoz in the cup, and Álvaro Cervera has called fitness a main worry; Mallorca needed extra time to beat Alcoyano in the cup and had two days to recover. Mallorca are without Morlanes, Antoniu Roca, David López, Antonio Sánchez and others (the listed ones are in the numbers), with Alberto Moreno and Puigmal doubts, while Raíllo, Valjent, Cerdà, Dani Luna and the returning internationals are available. Mallorca are in their worst spell (five games without a clean sheet) and their sporting director was dismissed this week; referee Juan Gordillo Escamilla shows many cards and the numbers already add for him.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals. Two points pull in opposite directions: Cervera's Tenerife defend deep and concede little and both teams are tired, but Mallorca have gone five games without a clean sheet and Enric Gallego is a constant threat. The numbers already count both sides' recent scoring, so I stay at 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners and already add for Mallorca's 43 corners in their last six. Tenerife sitting deep and breaking could feed Mallorca corners, but that is the pattern the numbers already see, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards, already raised a lot for referee Juan Gordillo Escamilla (7.8 a game in 6 games) and for both sides' recent cards. Tired legs late in the game can bring fouls, but the atmosphere around the De Miguel tribute has been one of respect between the clubs, so I add nothing and stay at 6.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.4 shots. I lean slightly lower to about 21.5 because Tenerife play their third game in six days and Mallorca had only two days after an extra-time cup tie, which the numbers can't see, and Cervera's side limits chances at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.7 shots on target. For the same fatigue reasons and Tenerife's tight defending, I trim it a little to about 6.5.

401882300.overall: Córdoba (10th, 20 points, five unbeaten) host Real Oviedo (9th, 21 points), with both chasing the play-off places three points away. Córdoba come off a 3-3 at Mallorca after leading 3-1; Iván Ania says only the long-term injured and Diarra are out and Kevin Medina is back in training. Oviedo have a new coach, Raúl González, in his second game after Julián Calero left on 9 November, and they are much better away (13 points) than at home; Pablo Sáenz hurt his calf on Thursday, Chris Ramos and Dani Calvo are long-term out (all three are in the numbers), Alberto Reina, who scored against Girona, is a doubt and Enzo Pérez is back from Spain Under-19 duty. Both sides have been in high-scoring, high-shot form and the numbers already count that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals, already adjusting for Oviedo's missing Sáenz, Calvo and Chris Ramos and both sides' strong recent scoring. Reina's doubt points slightly down for Oviedo while Córdoba's open games (3-3 at Mallorca) and Oviedo's good away form point the other way, so I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners and already add a lot for Córdoba's 48 corners in their last six. Ania says he does not know how Oviedo's new coach will set up away from home, so there is nothing firm to move on and I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards, already raised for both sides' recent card counts (23 and 21 in their last six). The referee was not yet named when I checked and I found no other new factor, so I stay at 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already raised well above a usual game for both teams' recent shooting (95 and 103 in their last six). A new coach adds some uncertainty to Oviedo's approach but no clear direction, so I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already boosted for both sides' recent accuracy. Enzo Pérez's return helps Oviedo while Reina may miss out, which roughly cancels, so I stay at 10.5.

401882298.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 points) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 points) under pressure from their own fans after more than a month without a home win; the players have vowed to win at El Molinón. Nicolás Larcamón has up to eight absences: Juan Otero and Álex Corredera are banned (Corredera's appeal was rejected) and Sarco is unlikely, which the numbers count, but Antonio Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García and Konrad are also injured and are not in the numbers, leaving the attack very thin with academy players called on. Las Palmas, improving under new coach Albert Sánchez, are without Opoku (banned) and several injured players the numbers know about, plus Ale García (knocks), who is not in them; Viti and Sergio Ruiz are close but not ready. The referee was not yet named when I checked.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already cut Sporting for Otero, Corredera and Sarco. I lean lower to about 2.1 because Sporting are also without forward Antonio Casas, Gelabert and Pablo García, so the attack rests on academy players and a barely fit Andrés Ferrari, and Las Palmas lose Ale García as well.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, close to both sides' recent levels. Sporting will push for a home win their fans demand, but with a weakened attack that does not clearly add corners, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards, raised for both sides' recent cards (21 each in their last six) and trimmed for two past meetings. Sporting's recent red cards (Corredera, Otero) and the tense home mood point up a little, but that is already in the momentum figures and the referee is not yet known, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, with a boost for Sporting's 86 shots in their last six. That form came with players now injured (Casas, Gelabert, Pablo García) on top of the counted absences, so I trim it to about 23.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. With Sporting's main forwards out and Las Palmas missing Ale García too, I lower it to about 7.9.

401883109.overall: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, so this is a direct fight for the play-off places; Eibar are on a five-game winless run but are the sixth-best away side, and Girona have taken only 10 of their points at home. Girona are short at the back: Àlex Moreno is banned for a fifth yellow and Furtado, Bryan Gil and Jastin García are injured (all in the numbers), but Javi Boñar is also injured and Holmes Junior Zamorano is away with Spain Under-18, which reports say leaves just four fit defenders and may mean a first league start for Abdul Mumin. Eibar under Jokin Aranbarri have nearly a full squad, with only Imanol, Bernat and Gift working in the gym. The referee was not yet named when I checked.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already add for Àlex Moreno's absence from Girona's defence. I lean slightly higher to about 2.3 because Girona are also without Boñar and Zamorano and may start Mumin, who has not started a league game this season after a long knee injury, against an Eibar side that has been creating plenty (35 shots on target in their last six).

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, already adding for Eibar conceding 44 corners in their last six. Nothing new points either way, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards, close to a usual game. Aleix Garrido expects a match of many duels and the play-off stakes are real, but the referee is not yet known and the numbers already count both sides' recent cards, so I stay at 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Girona's patched defence could give Eibar a little more, but Girona's attack (Vanat, Abel Ruiz, Carles Pérez) is intact, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. With Girona down to four fit defenders, beyond the ban the numbers count, Eibar's accurate recent shooting should find a little more, so I nudge it to about 9.4.

401883304.overall: Celta Fortuna (17th, 13 points, 6 points from their last 10 games) host Real Valladolid (12th, 18 points) at Balaídos; reports say coach Fredi Álvarez could be sacked if results don't improve. Celta's reserve side plays open, attacking football but has conceded 26 goals, the second most in the division; Álvaro Marín has 8 goals. Valladolid are without Thiago Ojeda (fifth yellow) and Juanmi Latasa (both in the numbers) and also Trilli (abductor tear, three to four weeks), who is not; Fran Escribá wants to avoid an end-to-end game and complained that too many yellows come from protests. The referee was not yet named when I checked.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already boosting Valladolid for 14 goals in their last six and trimming them for Latasa and Ojeda. I lean slightly lower to about 2.6 because Escribá has said he wants a controlled game, not the back-and-forth Celta Fortuna thrive on, although Celta's leaky defence keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and already add for Valladolid's recent corners (39 in six) against a Celta side that conceded 47. I found nothing new for corners, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.5 cards, raised for Celta's recent card count; both teams have collected many yellows and Ojeda misses out after his fifth. Escribá's complaint about protest cards may calm his side a little, but that is not enough to move, so I stay at 6.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, already lifted for Valladolid's recent shooting (88 in six) and Celta's openness. Escribá's caution points slightly down, Celta's young, fast side slightly up, so I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target, boosted for Valladolid's 39 on target in their last six. Valladolid's front four of Víctor Jr, Arnu, Abed and Ponceau is expected to stay unchanged, so nothing new points either way and I stay at 9.8.

401876395.overall: A relegation six-pointer opens the round: Troyes are 17th with 8 points and Le Havre last with 2 after six straight league defeats. Valérien Ismaël takes charge of Le Havre for the first time; his past sides pressed hard and he is still choosing between a back three and a back four. Le Havre's own preview lists Pembélé, Rassoul Ndiaye, Nakamura and Mosengo out and Ouziad doubtful, with Jelert back, while Mpasi, Mambimbi and Zagadou are long-term absentees. For Troyes, Junior Diaz is suspended (already counted) and forward Yacouba Koné is a doubt; Troyes have scored only 7 league goals, and Ligue 1's own figures show these two have the league's lowest shot conversion. Referee Jérémie Pignard (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers; no match-day news changed the view.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Troyes have scored just 7 in 10 league games and may lack forward Koné, and these are the two sides with the lowest shot conversion in Ligue 1, while Ismaël's first job will be to tighten a Le Havre side missing four midfielders. I go a little lower, to about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with Troyes at home doing most of the pushing. Neither side's style changes much for this: Troyes build slowly and Le Havre will defend deep under a coach in his first game, which the numbers already reflect, so I stay at 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and already add Pignard's strict record (+17%). On top of that this is a bottom-two scrap where both sides need points badly and Ismaël's teams are known for intensity and pressing, which the numbers' stakes flags do not cover; a small lift to about 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. Troyes create few big chances and Le Havre will be careful, but both will also have to chase points late on, so the two pull against each other and I stay at 24.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. Troyes have the league's weakest attack and may be without Koné, and Le Havre's forwards get little support with Ndiaye, Nakamura and Mosengo out, so I trim slightly to about 7.5.

401876398.overall: Leaders PSG (23 points, five straight league wins) visit sixth-placed Nice (17 points), who have won five of their last six league games under Olivier Pantaloni. Dembélé, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes and Akliouche are back in the PSG squad, but with Roma at the Parc on Wednesday the latest French reports (VIPSG, 433foot, Paris-Supporters) expect a reshuffled XI: Doué fully rested after a muscle alert with France, Hakimi and Pacho rested, and Mayulu, Ndjantou, Ferran Torres and Godts starting, with the returning stars on the bench. The numbers only take Kvaratskhelia off for PSG, so they still assume a near first-choice side. Nice are without Abdelmonem (hamstring) plus long-term absentees Bombito, Abergel and Mendy, all already counted, while Boudaoui and Abdi may return and Wahi leads the line. Referee Jérôme Brisard (4.2 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with PSG's strong scoring run and Kvaratskhelia's absence (-4%) already counted. Since yesterday the reports add Hakimi and Pacho to Doué among those rested, so PSG are expected to start without Doué, Hakimi and Kvaratskhelia and with Dembélé on the bench; I deepen my trim from -2 to -4, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, driven by PSG's possession against a Nice back three with wing-backs Clauss and Nkounkou. Rotation changes who attacks rather than how much PSG push Nice back, and Nice's form and missing defenders are already in the numbers, so I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards and already include Jérôme Brisard's slightly above-average record, Nice's recent rise in cards and PSG's low count. A younger PSG side could commit a few more fouls, but nothing points clearly to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, already raised for both sides' recent shooting. PSG will still have most of the ball, but a starting XI without Doué, Hakimi and Dembélé, the players who drive much of their shooting, should create a little less in the first hour; I cut to about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target and already give PSG +20% for 60 on target in their last six, a run built by the first-choice attack. With Doué rested and Dembélé expected on the bench, I trim to about 11.8.

401876399.overall: Monaco (7th, 16 points) have gone five league games without a win under Filipe Luís and have not kept a clean sheet in eight, while Auxerre (15th, 10 points) under Will Still have lost their last two, including 5-1 at Strasbourg, and have conceded a league-high 24 goals. Filipe Luís confirmed Golovin (calf), Idumbo and Ansu Fati are out, all counted by the numbers, with defender Mawissa a game-day decision on a groin problem; Coulibaly is available because his ban starts next round. Auxerre's striker Danny Namaso is ruled out with a swollen ankle (Camfoot, Eurofootnews), as the numbers already assumed, alongside Okoh, Dioussé, Fofana and Zaddy, with Oppegard doubtful and Dioubaté back from suspension. Filipe Luís expects a compact Auxerre that breaks fast through Archer and Faivre and says Monaco must take risks. Referee Jérémy Stinat (4.1 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take almost a fifth off Auxerre's attack for Namaso, now confirmed out, and some off Monaco for Golovin and Idumbo. Monaco's leaky defence and Auxerre's poor one are already in the numbers too, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Monaco expected to have most of the ball against Auxerre's back three and wing-backs. Filipe Luís wants more risk going forward, but that is how Monaco usually play at home, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add Stinat's slightly strict record and past meetings. Dioubaté returns for Auxerre and Coulibaly is available for Monaco, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots. Filipe Luís admits his attack has struggled without Golovin, which is already counted, and Auxerre will sit compact and counter; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. With Namaso out as the numbers assumed, Archer is Auxerre's main threat, and Monaco's finishing problems are already in their recent record, so I stay at 9.3.

401876403.overall: Lens (11th) and Toulouse (12th) are level on 13 points, but Lens come in after a 9-1 Champions League defeat at Como, two league defeats and the sacking of Yannick Cahuzac; Didier Digard takes charge for the first time. His first squad brings back Ganiou and Sima after weeks out, though both may start on the bench, but leaves out forward Franjo Ivanović and defender Jonathan Gradit (no reason given; Lensois says Ivanović was hurt late in the week), on top of Édouard, Bulatović and Nawrocki, who are counted. Toulouse (Jens Berthel Askou) miss Messali (counted) but have Dønnum, Amougou and Abu Francis back, with Tengstedt (five goals) leading the line. Referee Bastien Dechepy (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, partly because Lens have leaked heavily lately. Ivanović is now out too, which the numbers don't know, leaving Thauvin, Hazard and Sotoca with Sima only half-ready, and a new coach after a 9-1 defeat will want a solid first game; Gradit's absence at the back pulls slightly the other way, so I keep a small trim to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lens are expected in a 3-4-3 with wing-backs Aguilar and Udol and Digard wants play down the flanks, while Toulouse play a 4-4-2; that is close to how both usually play, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards and already add Dechepy's strict record (about +15%) and past meetings. A first game under a new coach brings energy but also more attention to discipline, and nothing points either way, so I stay at 4.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. Digard's pressing could add a few for Lens, but Toulouse create a lot without finishing and Lens are short of fit forwards; these balance out, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With Ivanović now left out, Sima not fully fit and Édouard injured (counted), Lens have less sharpness up front than the numbers allow for, so I trim a little more, to about 8.5.

401876402.overall: Second-placed Lille (21 points), the league's best defence and unbeaten in five, host fifth-placed Lyon (17 points), who have lost three away league games in a row. Lyon start under new coach Carlos Vicens, who keeps a 4-3-3; his first squad has Tagliafico, Kango and Himbert but not Clinton Mata (ruled out, not in the numbers), Openda, Sulc, Morton or Ouédraogo (all counted). For Lille, Davide Ancelotti confirmed Ayase Ueda is fit after a month out, though a start looks unlikely; the numbers never counted him as missing, so his return changes nothing, while Tiago Santos and Igamane are out and counted. Lille host Bayern in the Champions League next week, Lyon's fans are banned from travelling, and François Letexier (4.0 cards a game) referees, already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, with the missing forwards on both sides already taken off. I correct last night's reasoning: Ueda was never counted out, so his return is no reason to move; the small nudge now comes from Lyon losing right-back Mata, a regular the numbers don't know is missing, to about 2.24.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners. Both sides play a 4-3-3 with wide forwards, and Vicens has kept Lyon's back four, so I see no reason to move from 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, with Letexier's near-average record already in. Lyon's travelling fans are banned and nothing points to a heated game under a new Lyon coach, so I stay at 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots. Lille's possession game and Vicens wanting a higher press could add a few, but Lyon are without Openda and Sulc up front (counted), so I stay at 21.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Last night I nudged this up for Ueda, but the numbers already assumed him available, so I go back to 8.3; Lille's sharpness up front is as the numbers expect.

401876396.overall: Strasbourg (14th, 10 points, five defeats in six) sacked Hugo Oliveira this week and Vítor Matos, from Swansea, takes charge for the first time at the Meinau. Matos calls attacking football with pressing non-negotiable, but he confirmed Giovanni Reyna (scorer in the last game) and Oso will miss this one, on top of striker Panichelli; only Panichelli is counted by the numbers, and goalkeeper Jørgensen, a doubt after international duty, is now expected to start. Brest (9th, 15 points) arrive in form after beating Lorient and Lyon without conceding, missing only Chardonnet and Le Guen (counted), with Ajorque leading the line against his old club. Azzedine Souifi referees; the numbers know only four of his top-flight games and blend them with an average record.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, a high figure driven by Strasbourg's open games. Matos wants to attack, but he loses Reyna and Oso on top of Panichelli (only Panichelli is counted), so Strasbourg's attack is thinner than the numbers think; I trim slightly to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Both teams are expected in a 4-2-3-1 or 4-3-3, and a pressing start under Matos is close to how Strasbourg already play, so I stay at 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards. Souifi has only four games in the numbers, which already blend his record with an average referee, and Matos' pressing could bring a few fouls but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots. A new coach demanding intensity at home could add a few, while Reyna's and Oso's absences take some away, so I stay at 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Without Reyna, Oso and Panichelli, Strasbourg lose much of their finishing and creativity, more than the numbers count, so I trim slightly to about 8.6.

401876397.overall: Third-placed Paris FC (20 points, unbeaten in five at home) host Angers (16th, 8 points), who have one win in eight and have not scored in their last three. Liam Rosenior's side lean on Lassine Sinayoko, the league's top scorer with nine goals; reports differ on Ikoné, Sangui, Adama Camara and Chergui (one preview lists all four out, earlier news had them returning), and the numbers already count Ikoné and Sangui as missing. Angers (Stéphane Gilli, a former Paris FC coach) miss the suspended Lefort (counted) and Bané Diatta, with reports also listing striker El Ouazzani (adductor) and one player ill; Gilli says he will adjust defensively without a big overhaul. Angers are expected to sit deep, and referee Aurélien Petit (2.5 cards a game in four top-flight games) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already add a little for Lefort's absence in Angers' defence. Angers have not scored in three and may be without El Ouazzani, but Paris FC have conceded in each of their last three home games and Sinayoko is in form; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Against a deep, struggling Angers side Paris FC are likely to have long spells of pressure out wide through Kebbal and their wing-backs, which tends to produce corners, so I nudge it up to about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards and already take some off for Petit's lenient start. Gilli facing his former club adds a little edge, but nothing points to a heated game, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, with Paris FC doing most of the shooting, and they already add a lot for Paris FC's recent shooting and Angers' leaky last six games. Nothing new adds to that, so I stay at 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. Sinayoko is in form for Paris FC, while Angers have barely tested goalkeepers lately and may lack El Ouazzani; the numbers already see both trends, so I stay at 8.8.

401876401.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 points) and Rennes (8th, 16 points), one point apart. Lorient (Alexandre Dujeux) have one of the league's tightest defences, have won the last six league meetings and beat Le Havre 2-0 before the break; Katseris is out and Isaak Touré and Ibrahima Baldé are doubts, all three counted out by the numbers. Rennes have lost three of their last four and dropped from first to eighth; Franck Haise answered public criticism from chairman Nicolas de Tavernost, and top scorer Estéban Lepaul (seven goals) is back in training and a candidate for the squad after an ankle injury, while Frankowski is out (counted) and Rongier travels after a precautionary rest. The numbers do not flag this as a derby, and Marc Bollengier (4.1 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals. Lorient's tight defence is already in them, but Lepaul, Rennes' top scorer, is back after missing the games the numbers learned from, and Touré and Baldé are only doubts though counted out, so I lean slightly higher, to about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Lorient's 3-4-2-1 and Rennes' 3-5-2 both rely on wing-backs, which the numbers already reflect, and Rennes having to break down a compact block is how this fixture usually goes, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards with Bollengier's record in, but they do not treat this as a derby. Breton derbies are usually fierce and Rennes are under pressure from their chairman after a poor run, so I add a little, to about 4.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots. Lepaul's return helps Rennes' finishing more than their number of shots, and Lorient's compact style is unchanged, so I stay at 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. A sharp striker like Lepaul back in the squad should put a few more efforts on target, though he may start on the bench, so I nudge it up only to about 9.2.

401882805.overall: Athletic (7th, 16 pts, a game in hand) host Espanyol (13th, 12 pts) on Friday night at San Mamés; a win would lift them into 6th. The main match-day change: Aitor Paredes is back in Terzic's 23-man squad after muscle discomfort, along with Nico Serrano, while Yeray, Yuri and Berenguer rejoined full training; Vivian (soleus), Guruzeta, Sannadi and Egiluz stay out. The numbers still take Paredes off, so part of that cut comes back. Espanyol miss Kike García and Calatrava, Urko is a serious doubt and Carreras awaits clearance, while Expósito (counted as out) and Puado are close; Eder Sarabia, appointed on 28 October, sits on the bench after a ban and has taken four points from two games. Mateo Busquets Ferrer referees; the numbers already add a lot for his high card record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and take about 8% off Athletic's scoring because they count Aitor Paredes as out. He is now in the squad (named in Friday's list, per FútbolFantasy and ElDesmarque) and likely to start with Vivian injured, so most of that cut comes back; with Puado fit for Espanyol I go up 5% (was 2%), to about 2.31 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, 6.4 of them Athletic's, and already add Athletic's corners against an Espanyol side that conceded 44 in their last six games. Sarabia wants Espanyol to keep the ball more, but two games are too few to say they will concede fewer corners, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.6 cards: they add about 29% for referee Busquets Ferrer (5.8 cards a game on their record) and about 9% for Espanyol's heavy recent card count (20 in six), most of it under the previous, more combative set-up. The referee is already counted, so I keep only a mild trim for the change of style, to about 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, 17.7 of them Athletic's, and already add Athletic's busy recent shooting (94 in six games). Nothing new moves it, so 26.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and already take some off Espanyol for their poor recent accuracy (18 on target in six). Roberto Fernández (six goals) and a fit Puado give Espanyol a little more threat than in recent weeks, but Athletic concede few chances at home. These balance, so I stay at 8.4.

401882806.overall: Alavés (13th, 13 pts, no league win in eight) host Deportivo (9th, 15 pts) at Mendizorroza at 14:00 on Saturday. Alavés miss Mikel Rodríguez and Facundo Garcés for the season (both in the numbers), while Abde and Mariano only rejoined training on Friday and are unlikely to start; Quique Sánchez Flores is expected to keep a five-man defence with intense pressing. goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already trim Alavés for their poor scoring run (4 in six) and for Mikel Rodríguez. They don't see that Deportivo are without striker Zakaria and that Aubameyang, scorer of a third of their goals, may only make the bench after his ankle knock; since he did travel and the club calls it minor, I trim a little less than yesterday, to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners and already take some off Alavés for their low recent count (19 in six games) while adding for Deportivo's busy run (41). Deportivo's wide play through Yeremay and Luismi Cruz doesn't depend on Aubameyang, and an Alavés side defending in a back five rarely changes the corner pattern, so I keep 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards: they now include referee García Verdura, who averages 4.3 cards a game (below the league's 4.7), and both sides' quiet recent card counts. shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots and already add about 16% to Deportivo for their heavy recent shooting (96 in six). Zakaria is out and Aubameyang may play only part of the game, so Deportivo lose some of their penalty-box shooting; a small trim to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target, with Alavés' poor recent accuracy and Deportivo's good run already counted. Aubameyang is Deportivo's most accurate finisher and his minutes are uncertain, with Zakaria not travelling, so I trim slightly to about 8.3.

401882799.overall: Rayo (14th, 12 pts, no away win but 10 points from five home games) host Valencia (19th, 9 pts) at Vallecas on Saturday afternoon, with Valencia in the drop zone and four of the last five meetings drawn. Rayo miss Batalla, Luiz Felipe and Óscar Valentín (in the numbers), and Álvaro García, Vertrouwd and Kumbulla are doubts; Camello (seven league goals) leads the line. goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals and already add for Gayà's ban and take a little off for the many draws between these sides. Danjuma is back in training, possibly for minutes off the bench, and Rayo may lack Álvaro García's width; these are small and pull both ways, so I stay at 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners and already add some for Valencia conceding plenty lately (39 in six games). Maffeo playing out of position at left-back could let Ratiu and De Frutos reach the byline, but Álvaro García's doubt may cost Rayo some width on the other flank, so I keep 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards; they now include referee Munuera Montero (4.6 a game over 44 games, a light 3.0 yellows a game this season) and add about 13% for Valencia's heavy recent card count. Yesterday I trimmed for him because the numbers had no referee; now that they count him, trimming again would count him twice, and a tense relegation fight points the other way, so I stay at 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots and already add about 22% to Rayo for their heavy shooting against a Valencia side that concedes many attempts. Danjuma's possible return and Álvaro García's doubt roughly cancel, so I keep 29.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target, with Rayo's recent form already counted. Camello is in good scoring form and Sadiq is expected to start for Valencia, as the numbers assume; nothing new changes either attack, so I stay at 8.4.

401882797.overall: The Seville derby: Sevilla (6th, 18 pts, one win in five) host Betis (4th, 26 pts) at the Pizjuán at 18:30 on Saturday, with Betis away in Europe on Tuesday. Sevilla's 24-man squad has Peque and Fofana back, but Alfon, Carmona (both in the numbers), Marcão and Miguel Sierra are out, and García Plaza has said he will likely swap a striker for a third midfielder. goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already take off Morante and Ceballos for Betis. Cucho is back in the squad and Peque returns for Sevilla, but Sevilla lose centre-back Marcão and plan a more cautious three-man midfield; these offset, so I stay at 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners and already take some off Sevilla for their low recent count (19 in six). García Plaza's extra midfielder may mean less wide play, but Peque's return and Betis' wingers Antony and Abde keep both flanks busy; nothing clear moves it, so 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.7 cards, already including a large derby boost (about +39%) and Sánchez Martínez's record of about 4.5 cards a game. Bernal, a combative midfielder, is back from his ban, but the heat of a Seville derby is exactly what the boost already counts, so I add nothing and stay at 6.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots and already add Betis' busy recent shooting (97 in six) and Sevilla conceding plenty. Sevilla's coach plans to drop a striker for a third midfielder, which should slow the game a little, but Peque is back, so I trim only slightly, to about 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and already add Betis' good recent accuracy. A more cautious Sevilla shape pulls down a little, but Cucho and Riquelme, who scored three in his last two games, are both in Betis' squad; these offset, so I stay at 9.2.

401882798.overall: Real Madrid (2nd, 30 pts, eight straight wins in all competitions) host Celta (11th, 13 pts, no league win since mid-October, with 0-0s against Betis and Levante) on Saturday night, three points behind Barcelona. Vinícius is back from his ban and Mbappé, who has scored in seven straight club games, is fit; Rodrygo and Asencio are out (Rodrygo in the numbers) and Tchouaméni is listed as a doubt after adductor discomfort with France. Adrián Cordero Vega referees at the league average of 4.7 cards a game, already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals (2.2 Madrid, 0.8 Celta), with Madrid's 19 goals in their last six already counted. Celta lose Borja Iglesias up front and Miguel Román in midfield, which takes something off their 0.8, but losing centre-back Starfelt should give Mbappé and Vinícius more room; those cancel, so I stay at 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, already trimmed because both sides have won and conceded fewer corners than usual lately. Madrid should pin a weakened Celta back, but they attack mainly through the middle and in transition rather than from crosses, so I keep 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, lowered because both sides have been booked less than usual lately (Celta only 6 in six). Cordero Vega averages the league norm and the numbers count him; with no derby or table edge and Celta likely to sit deep, nothing points to a heated game, so I keep 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots and already add Madrid's heavy recent shooting (108 in six). Madrid have Vinícius back and almost the whole squad, while Celta lose Miguel Román in midfield and Starfelt at the back, which the numbers don't know, so Madrid should have even more of the ball; a small lean up to about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with Madrid's recent accuracy (50 on target in six) already counted. Mbappé is in scoring form, Vinícius returns, and Celta's back line is thinner than the numbers know without Starfelt; a small lean up to about 10.7.

401882804.overall: Leaders Barcelona (33 pts, the league's best attack) host Villarreal (8th, 15 pts) at 14:00 on Sunday, before a Champions League trip to Sabah on Wednesday. Rodri, Xavi Espart and Bardghji are out (in the numbers), but Koundé, Cubarsí and Olmo all trained with the group this week, so Flick should have almost his full defence; Olmo may start on the bench. goals.text: The numbers say 4.3 goals, already high, with Barcelona's scoring run and their absences counted. Yesterday I leaned up because Koundé and Cubarsí were doubts; both have now trained with the group, which tightens Barcelona's back line, while Villarreal's missing Foyth (looser defence) and Gerard Moreno (weaker attack) roughly cancel, so I go back to 4.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners and already add Villarreal's high recent corner count (41 in six). Barcelona will dominate the ball with Lamine Yamal and Raphinha driving wide, and Villarreal's wingers Moleiro and Pépé are fit; nothing changes either side's approach, so I stay at 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards and already add Villarreal's busy recent card record (15 in six). No referee has been named and the match has no derby or table edge; Renato Veiga is one booking from a ban, which may make him careful. I keep 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, with both sides' recent shooting already added. Barcelona's attack is fully fit, but Flick may manage minutes before Wednesday's trip, with Olmo likely on the bench; these roughly balance, so I stay at 28.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, already raised for Barcelona's recent accuracy (40 on target in six). Villarreal without Gerard Moreno create a little less, but Barcelona's finishing is at full strength; no clear reason to move it, so 10.6.

401882800.overall: Promoted Racing (10th, 14 pts, 11 of them at home) host in-form Real Sociedad (5th, 22 pts) at El Sardinero on Sunday afternoon. Racing's games have averaged almost 4 goals, they have conceded the most in the league (30) and have yet to keep a clean sheet, while Real Sociedad have scored in six straight league games but conceded in 12 straight away games. Racing miss Mantilla and Andrés Martín, and Maguette Gueye is unlikely after hamstring discomfort (all in the numbers); top scorer Zabiri is back from Morocco after 130 minutes. goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals and take off Barrenetxea, Andrés Martín and Gueye, plus a little for Yangel Herrera, who is in fact back from Venezuela duty rather than injured. Racing have not kept a clean sheet all season and Real Sociedad keep conceding away, so a slight lean up to about 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, already trimmed for Real Sociedad's lower recent corner count. Racing attack down the wings with Íñigo Vicente and Iker Luque, and Real Sociedad use Guedes and Kubo wide; nothing new changes that, so I keep 11.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and already add Racing's high recent card count (18 in six). Neither side has anyone suspended, the game has no derby or table edge and no referee has been named, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots and already add both sides' busy recent shooting (94 and 96 in six). Two open, attacking teams trading chances is what the numbers already show; Real Sociedad's late-returning internationals and the Palace game could bring some rotation, but that is too uncertain to size, so 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Zabiri and Óskarsson, both scoring regularly, are expected to play despite their late returns, as the numbers assume, and Sučić is over his tonsillitis; no change, 10.4.

401882801.overall: Osasuna (16th, 12 pts) host bottom side Málaga (20th, 5 pts) at El Sadar on Sunday evening in a game both badly need. Osasuna miss goalkeeper Aitor Fernández and Bretones (in the numbers); Budimir is back from Croatia duty, Oroz and Herrando are available but short of rhythm, and winger Del Castillo trained with the group on Friday but has played only 34 minutes this season and Arrasate is avoiding risks with him. goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already give Málaga a small boost for Bretones being out. Osasuna have scored only 12 in 12, Del Castillo is unlikely to be risked from the start, and a nervous relegation game tends to be cautious; since he is back in group training I trim only a little, to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts already counted. Osasuna lean on crosses from Rubén García and Moi Gómez for Budimir, which brings corners, and Málaga will need to attack; it balances out, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards; they add Osasuna's recent cards (19 in six) and take some off Málaga's quieter run, but make no adjustment for the stakes. A relegation fight against a bottom side that must take risks tends to be scrappy, so a small lean up to about 4.8; no referee named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting and how much each concedes (+11% each). A nervy game and Del Castillo's limited role point a little lower, but Budimir being fit and Málaga needing to attack point the other way, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Budimir is fit after the break, as the numbers assume, and Málaga's recent accuracy (33 on target in six) is already counted; no clear reason to move it, so 9.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. City should have most of the ball at home after three defeats, while Fulham defend in a 4-2-3-1 and rely on Robinson and Castagne getting forward; Nunes possibly missing changes the right-back but not the pattern, so I stay at about 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards, already counting referee Thomas Bramall (3.8 a game, below the 4.0 average) and Fulham's busier recent card count. No suspensions on either side and the stakes are ordinary ones for a Fulham side two points clear of the bottom three, so about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots, already adding about 6% to City for the shots Fulham have conceded lately. City react to a losing run at home with Haaland, Doku and Cherki expected to start, while Fulham have the league's thinnest scoring record; nothing here goes beyond what is counted, so I keep about 25.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, with Semenyo's absence already counted. Haaland is fit and Fulham's front line (García, King, Iwobi, Bobb) is intact with King over his groin tightness, so I stay at about 8.8.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already counting Bournemouth's hot scoring run and Forest's thin attack (5 goals in six, 9 from about 16 xG all season). Williams and Schlager remain doubts the numbers don't know about, and Diomande and Sangaré arrive back late after flight cancellations; Ndoye's return softens that, so I keep the small trim to about 2.65.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, already including Forest's recent rise in bookings and a near-average figure for referee Adam Herczeg. A direct, second-ball game with Forest near the bottom can get physical, but there is no derby, suspension or other story beyond what is counted, so about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Williams and Schlager being doubts and two travel-delayed midfielders weaken Forest's supply a little more than the numbers know, while Bournemouth are at full strength as usual, so a small trim to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already marking Forest down for poor recent accuracy (about -10%). The same Forest doubts take a touch more off their side, while Evanilson and Tavernier keep Bournemouth's threat steady: about 8.0.

Hudson-Odoi and Domínguez are out (counted), Schlager (thigh) and Neco Williams (ankle) are doubts the numbers don't count, Savona is back training but unlikely to start, and Muñoz, Diomande and Sangaré had disrupted travel back from international duty. goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already take a big chunk off Sunderland for losing Brobbey (about -23% on their goals). Emery has Manzambi and Wan-Bissaka available and the rest of the squad ready, so the earlier worry about Villa's doubts is gone; Alderete's return helps Sunderland's back line a little, so with no clear push either way I stay at 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Villa will have most of the ball and Sunderland are expected to sit in a 4-5-1 and break through Talbi and Le Fée; nothing in the team news changes that shape, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, already counting referee Andy Madley (3.7 a game) and Sunderland's recent rise in bookings. Alderete is back from his ban but there is no derby or other edge to the game, so about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, pushed up by both sides' recent shot volume. With Galatasaray away on Tuesday Emery may still manage minutes, and Sunderland lack a fit recognised top scorer, but his squad is now fully fit, so I cut the trim from 4% to 2%: about 27.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Villa's attacking players are all available after Emery's update, with Manzambi fit behind Jackson, and Sunderland's weaker attack without Brobbey and Xhaka is already in the numbers, so I stay at about 8.5.

Manzambi has recovered from his calf problem and Wan-Bissaka is back after six games out, so only Cash (concussion, counted), Onana and Ruggeri are missing. They don't know Gittens is also out, so Chelsea may play without a recognised striker, with Estevao or Neto central, after scoring little in the games without Pedro; against Leeds' tight defence (eight conceded in ten) I keep a mild trim to about 2.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already counting Michael Oliver (4.0 a game over 84 games, the league average) and Leeds' recent rise in bookings. Neither side has a suspension and the stakes are ordinary mid-table ones, so about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots, with Chelsea's recent dip in shot volume already in their momentum. Chelsea will have plenty of the ball and take speculative efforts even without a striker in form, so Gittens' absence affects quality more than volume; about 24.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Chelsea managed only two on target at Sunderland despite 69% possession, and with Gittens now confirmed out as well as Pedro, their finishers are thin against a well-organised Leeds; a small trim to about 8.7.

401879236.overall: Chelsea are fifth under Xabi Alonso after losing 1-0 at Sunderland before the break, a game in which they had most of the ball but little end product; Leeds are ninth under Daniel Farke, two points behind, have conceded only eight league goals and beat Tottenham 1-0 last time out. Michael Oliver referees, exactly at the league average for cards (counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already counting Mateta's ban and Palace's leaky recent defence and Coventry's good scoring run. corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Frank's sides like set pieces and direct play, but one week of training won't change Palace's wing-back system much, and Coventry's home style is already in their figures, so I stay at about 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, low for a game between 17th and 20th, already counting referee Darren England (4.2 a game). shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, pushed up by how many shots Palace have been conceding lately. Frank's first job will be to stop that, and Palace's own volume may suffer with Nketiah rather than Mateta or Strand Larsen up front: about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. A more cautious first game under Frank and a Palace attack without Mateta, Sarr and probably a starting Strand Larsen trims it a little, to about 7.8.
