Referee Darren England is slightly above average for cards (counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already taking about 6% off Spurs for Tel. What they can't see is Savio and Bergvall, whom they treat as out, being fit, and Maddison ready to start after Spurs missed his creativity at Leeds, against an Ipswich side without a clean sheet all season and with nine straight meetings of three goals or more; a mild lean up to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, with Spurs' high recent corner count (48 in six) and Ipswich's low one (14 in six) already in the momentum adjustment. Savio's wide play fits Spurs' style but he is likely to start on the bench, so about 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already adding about 12% for referee Robert Jones and Ipswich's slightly higher card count lately. O'Neil wants an aggressive approach, but there's no derby edge and no suspension story on either side, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, already adding about 15% to Spurs for their 104 shots in the last six. Maddison and Savio returning add quality more than extra volume on top of a figure already pushed high, so I keep 28.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. With Maddison confirmed fit to start and Savio (nearly three chances created a game) available, Spurs should turn more efforts on target than in the Leeds defeat without them: about 9.0.

401878754.overall: Spurs (11th) host Ipswich (14th) after a 1-0 defeat at Leeds ended a run of three straight wins under Roberto De Zerbi. Maddison, Savio and Bergvall were all late fitness checks during the week, and Friday's update was that all three are fit, with Maddison likely to start; the numbers still list Savio and Bergvall as out, and only Tel's absence is sized by them. Tel, Mudryk and Adarabioyo are not ready, and Xavi Simons and Odobert remain out. Ipswich, under Gary O'Neil, have won one of their last seven in all competitions, have a fully fit squad and have not kept a clean sheet all season; the last nine meetings all had three goals or more. Referee Robert Jones (4.3 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

401879232.overall: Leaders Arsenal (27 points, five straight league wins and four straight clean sheets) visit 12th-placed Newcastle, who drew 1-1 at Fulham before the break and lost their last two home league games 1-0 without scoring, to Villa and Everton. Arteta has Zubimendi out with a hamstring injury from Spain duty, Saka (quad) still weeks away and Max Dowman serving the last game of his ban, all of which the numbers count; Saliba is close but his minutes are being built up and Konsa faced a late fitness check. Newcastle are without Joelinton and goalkeeper Jaouen (counted), while Ramsey is back from his ban and Nico González, Willock and Fernández-Pardo are over illness. Referee Chris Kavanagh (4.5 cards a game) is already in the numbers. Match-day previews add nothing new: Kavanagh is confirmed, both sides' expected line-ups are close to full strength apart from the listed absences, and Arsenal's Champions League game midweek has not led to any announced rotation.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 11% off Arsenal for Saka and lowering Newcastle for their poor scoring lately (6 goals in six, none in their last two home games). Arsenal's four clean sheets in a row point lower, but Zubimendi's absence takes some control out of their midfield and Newcastle get Ramsey, Willock and González back; those pull in both directions, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Arsenal pin teams back and both sides are dangerous from set pieces, but that is in their ratings and recent counts (Arsenal 36 corners in six games), and Zubimendi's absence is not the kind of change that alters how much either side attacks down the flanks, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already adding about 21% for referee Chris Kavanagh and more for both sides' busier recent card counts. A home crowd frustrated with Jaissle and an Arsenal midfield without its usual holding man could mean more fouls, but that is a hunch the counts mostly cover already, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots, already raised for Newcastle conceding plenty of shots lately and Arsenal's steady volume. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target, already lowered for Newcastle's poor recent accuracy (21 on target in six). Saka's absence is counted and the only new forward news is Fernandez-Pardo being available again after a virus, which is too small to move it, so I stay at 7.8.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already adding about 12% to United for their busy attacking under Carrick (96 shots in six). 401878755.overall: Liverpool (4th, 18 points) host Manchester United (18th, one league win all season) in the derby, and it is Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge after Michael Carrick's sacking; he only started on 18 November and is expected to keep Carrick's 4-2-3-1 with a mid-block rather than risk a high press. Liverpool under Andoni Iraola have won only one of five home league games but are dangerous on the break; van Dijk has trained, Gravenberch is managing heel pain and Frimpong is back in training, while Ekitiké, Bradley and Leoni are out. United are without Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte (counted) and Luke Shaw is injured, leaving Amass or Dorgu at left-back, while Lisandro Martínez is back from a ban and Maguire recovered from a back spasm. The derby boost to cards (about +39%) and referee Sam Barrott (4.1 cards a game) are already in the numbers.

401875056.overall: Como (5th, 23 points, four straight wins before a 2-0 defeat at Inter) host Cagliari (9th, 16 points), who ended a run of four defeats with a 1-0 win at Frosinone before the break. Como are without Kean (a tibia setback that will keep him out for weeks), Jesus Rodriguez, Addai and Diao, all on the numbers' list, while Chalobah is hoped to be back; the probable side has Paz, Da Cunha and Baturina behind Douvikas. Referee Andrea Calzavara's low card record (3.0 a game) is already in the numbers, and this morning's checks found nothing new, so the view stays with the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already lifted for Como's hot scoring run (+6%) and cut for Diao (-8%) and Kean (-2%). Chalobah's likely return tightens Como's defence while Cagliari still miss Mina and play one striker, which is about what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, mostly Como's (5.9), as they keep the ball against a Cagliari side that will defend deep. Without Diao and Addai Como lose some width, but both have been out for a while and that is already in their recent corner numbers, so I stay at about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already count Calzavara's low rate (3.0 a game) and both teams' quiet recent run (Como only 4 cards in six games). Cagliari will press Como's midfield at times, but there is no rivalry and no suspension threat reported, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, with Como taking about 18. Como's probable attack (Paz, Da Cunha, Baturina behind Douvikas) is the one that has been shooting a lot, and Cagliari's deep block is how they usually play away, so I stay at about 26.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already raised for Como's sharp recent shooting (+13%). Mina is out as the numbers assume and Obert's return only changes Cagliari's left side, so nothing new pushes it either way and I stay at about 9.1.

401874981.overall: Unbeaten leaders Lazio (29 points, a club record start under Gattuso) host Lecce (14th, 10 points, three defeats in their last four before the break and among the league's lowest scorers). Zaccagni, Nuno Tavares, Sutalo and Marusic are out, as the numbers assume, so Noslin and Pedraza fill the left side and Doekhi or Provstgaard partners Diogo Leite; Frattesi has recovered from his fatigue with Italy and should start, and Gudmundsson and Rovella are fit for the bench. For Lecce, Pierotti and Ilic are out, while Monteiro and Berisha were still on individual work this week and are doubtful; the numbers now treat Monteiro as available, so a late absence would only take a little off Lecce. goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already cut for Zaccagni (-10.5%) and Tavares (-6%) and raised on Lecce's side for Lazio's missing defenders. Frattesi, Lazio's joint top scorer with four, is fit, and Lecce's doubt over Monteiro is small for a side that scores little, so I stay at about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Without Zaccagni and Tavares Lazio lose their most direct left side, while Lecce have won plenty of corners lately (33 in six); the numbers already see the absences and the form, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards and already add Marcenaro's high rate (+19%) while taking some off for Lazio's calm recent run. Lecce need points and will press, which can bring fouls, but there is no rivalry or suspension threat, so I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Lazio's front three of Isaksen, Pinamonti and Noslin with Frattesi arriving from midfield is close to their recent attack, so I stay at about 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target, with Lecce's sharp recent shooting (34 on target in six) already counted. Frattesi being fit and Monteiro being doubtful pull slightly against each other, so I stay at about 8.7.

Gilardino's defence is in an emergency: Ndiaye is suspended and Diego Carlos has an adductor strain (both on the numbers' list), but Drobnic is also short of fitness, Valenti is out of the squad and Bernabe is a big doubt, which leaves Delprato, Troilo and Carboni as the only fit centre-backs or forces a back four that failed against Bologna. Referee Simone Sozza (4.2 cards a game) is already in the numbers. corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add Roma's strong recent corner count (+9%). Roma's wing-backs Molina and Wesley push high and Parma will sit deep, but that pattern is already in Roma's recent figures, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add Sozza's above-average record (4.2 a game, +13%). There is no rivalry and Roma have been fairly clean lately (counted); Parma's makeshift defence may need to foul more, but not enough for me to move, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already raised a lot for Roma's recent shooting (+26%). A weakened Parma defence points up, but Parma's own attack without Romero shoots little and the figure is already high, so I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target and already lift Roma for their recent accuracy (+13%). Dybala adds finishing quality the recent games lacked, against a Parma back line short of fit centre-backs beyond the two the numbers know about; a small nudge to about 9.6.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already cut for Lobotka and Di Lorenzo and raised for Meret's absence and Napoli's leaky defence (14 conceded in six). cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already add Rapuano's high rate (+32%). Both sides have been fairly calm lately, nobody is near a ban that has been reported and there is no rivalry angle in the previews, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, already lifted for Torino's shooting against a Napoli side that has allowed many chances. Without De Bruyne from the start Napoli lose some long-range shooting, but Gilmour and McTominay still push forward and Napoli must chase the win, so I stay at about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. De Bruyne, Napoli's best finisher this season, is now expected on the bench and Vlasic is doubtful for Torino, which takes a little quality off both attacks; a small trim to about 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards, cut for both teams' quiet recent run (about -10% and -13%) and for Arena's low record on just three games. shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target, almost all of the change in Juve's hands (6.0). Juve's expected front three is their usual one and their recent accuracy is already counted, so I stay at about 8.9.

Davis, Udinese's main striker, is still a real doubt and Bologna lose Miranda's crossing from the left, with Cambiaghi also unsure, none of which the numbers count; a mild lean down to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Bologna's wide play goes on through Zortea and Alhassane, and Udinese under Zanetti defend with a back three, close to what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count Marinelli's average record. Udinese have been calm (7 cards in six) and Zanetti wants more bite in duels, which could add a foul or two, but nothing clear points either way, so I stay at about 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Miranda's absence costs Bologna an attacking outlet and a Udinese side without Davis would have little up front, which the numbers don't know; a small nudge down to about 25.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, already raised for Bologna's sharp recent shooting (+16%). Orsolini and Odgaard are expected to lead the line as usual, so I stay at about 8.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. A more cautious Sassuolo might defend deeper and give Genoa more, but Genoa have won few corners lately (20 in six), so the two pull in opposite directions; I stay at about 8.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. D'Aversa's first priority is a more compact side after 29 goals conceded, and De Rossi's Genoa are also well organised, which points to a slower game with fewer chances; a small trim to about 24.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, already low for Sassuolo's poor shooting lately (14 on target in six). A more cautious game points down, a possible Berardi return points up, so I stay at about 8.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, already raised for Frosinone's big recent corner count (+9.5%). Milan's makeshift defence doesn't change how either side gets to the byline, so I stay at about 9.9.

Jonathans and Ohio are out long term; Correia said today that Engwanda, Paredes and Jensen are back in the group but not yet match-fit, so at most they could come off the bench, while the numbers count them as out. Cambuur's main threat is Utrecht loanee Rafik El Arguioui; they miss Amofa, Visser and Westerhof, Asselman is still unlikely, and Sports Mole expects Jansen in goal. Referee Allard Lindhout (3.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already counting Cambuur's scoring run (16 in six) and Utrecht's leaky defence (15 conceded in six). shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already including Excelsior giving up many on-target shots and barely hitting the target themselves (9 in six). cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already including a large derby boost (+39%) and Alex Bos' 3.3 cards a game. goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, counting Mendes out for Telstar (-3.5%) and defender Alders out (+6% for PEC). corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (25 in six) already counted. Pastoor has said the squad needs little changing, and Telstar's wing play through Martha and Brouwer is what they have shown all season, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's slightly busier recent card count. It is a tense six-pointer near the bottom, but that is normal at this end of the table and no bans or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already lifted for Telstar's busy recent shooting (+11%), led by Tyrone Owusu. A possible Mendes return adds an option but not a big change in volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target, with both sides' recent accuracy close to normal. A new coach's first game can be cautious, but Pastoor says he is building on the side that went four unbeaten, so I see no reason to move and stay at 10.6.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts, two behind PSV, best defence in the league) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, a league-high 40 goals conceded and a league-low 11 scored. Willem II coach Jurgen Streppel wants his side to try to play out of Twente's press while staying compact; captain Justin Hoogma (knee) and Amine Lachkar (groin) are out (counted) and keeper Thomas Didillon is doubtful, with Delanghe expected to start. goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, already lifted for Twente's 21 goals in their last six and Willem II's 21 conceded. Thorvaldsen is out again, but Twente scored freely without him, and Willem II probably lose first-choice keeper Didillon, which pulls the other way, so I stay at 4.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, already up for Twente's 46 corners in six (+6%) and down for Willem II's low output. Streppel expects to be pushed back, which is exactly the one-sided pattern those figures describe, so I stay at 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with Serdar Gozubuyuk's 3.9 a game (+37%) and Willem II's 12 cards in six already counted. A side defending deep for long spells picks up cards, but that is priced in and no suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.6 shots, already lifted strongly for Twente's 145 shots in six (+25%) and cut for Willem II's low output. Streppel wants to keep the ball more and Twente may ease off with Freiburg on Thursday, but a home side this dominant rarely changes much, so I stay at 35.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, already up for Twente's accuracy (+14%) and down for Willem II's (-9%). Twente's absences are ones they have played without for weeks and Weghorst should lead the line, so I stay at 11.2.

401875547.overall: Third-placed Ajax (25 pts) host ADO Den Haag (17th, 9 pts) in Maurice Steijn's first game as ADO coach, after a full international break to prepare; ADO have not beaten Ajax in 20 meetings. goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals with Brandt taken off completely (-13% for Ajax, about -0.3 goals). corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Ajax's slightly low recent count and ADO's normal output already counted. Ajax will have most of the ball and Michel wants more pressing energy, which the 6.7 home corners already reflect, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, already nudged up for both sides' recent cards and down for Erwin Blank's lighter touch (-5%). No suspensions or flashpoints are reported, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, already up for Ajax's recent volume (+9%) and ADO's (+7%). Brandt starting and Berghuis on the bench add quality more than volume, and a compact ADO under Steijn may shoot less, so I stay at 34.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target with Brandt ruled out. With him expected to start and Berghuis available from the bench, Ajax have more chance creation than the numbers assume; +3% to about 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already pushed up for Sparta's 14 cards in six (+8%) and for Ingmar Oostrom (3.3 a game). Martes is one booking from a ban and may hold back a little, but no suspensions or extra needle are reported, so I stay at 3.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners. Le Mans' back five and Marseille's narrow attacking midfield (Harit, Abdelli) are already in the numbers, so I stay at 8.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, boosted strongly for Burgos' 98 shots in their last six. Without Karrikaburu and González, and against an Albacete side that now sits deeper and concedes fewer chances, I trim it slightly to about 25.4.
